title: Quality on the policy's own outputs, the nightly fuzz, and the gate again
purpose: Measure both math verifiers on rollouts the red-team policy actually wrote (labelled by the evaluation verifier, which shares no code with either), run the nightly fuzzing CronJob now against fresh policy outputs, and re-apply the gate to the strict verifier with its policy-output evidence.

steps.display: vq.py job pq-math-final-answer-1-0-0 -- policyq --verifier math-final-answer@1.0.0 --run red-lenient   # the last 10 steps' rollouts
vq.py job pq-math-final-answer-2-0-0 -- policyq --verifier math-final-answer@2.0.0 --run red-lenient   # the last 10 steps' rollouts
precision: natural answers in the gold set vs the policy's own outputs

checks.description: the old verifier is precise on natural answers, and on the policy's outputs its precision lower bound falls below the gate's 0.95
checks.because: The policy was trained against it and found what the gold set did not test.

checks.description: the strict verifier's precision lower bound on the same outputs stays above 0.95
checks.because: Its contract rejects the shapes the red-team policy learned; the few disagreements with the evaluation verifier are contract differences, listed in the stored record.

checks.description: the nightly job fuzzed with the policy's own completions, and found false positives only in the old verifiers
checks.because: Mutations are built around real policy text, so new behaviour opens new cases.

checks.description: the strict verifier is approved again, now with precision measured on policy outputs
checks.because: The gate takes the lower bound of precision on both populations.
